evaluations.query: speaker diarization pretrained model for audio segmentation, identify speaker turns with timestamps
evaluations.reason: Methods A and B both have GT at #1. Method A adds the older pyannote/speaker-diarization at #2 (showing version lineage) and nvidia streaming sortformer at #3. Method B has the community version and nvidia streaming. Method C misses GT entirely — pyannote community at #1 and nvidia sortformer variants are decent but lack the best-in-class GT.

evaluations.query: monocular depth estimation model that produces dense per-pixel depth maps from a single RGB image, no stereo input needed
evaluations.reason: Method C has GT DepthPro-hf at #1 and Depth-Anything-V2-Large-hf at #2 — both transformers-ready, plus the non-hf Depth-Anything at #3. Method B has DepthPro (non-hf) at #1 and GT at #2, plus Depth-Anything. Method A has GT at #1 but marigold-normals at #3 is surface normals estimation, not depth — a notable miss for a technically precise query.

evaluations.query: multimodal multilingual document retrieval model that jointly encodes text and visual layout for cross-lingual search over mixed-content pages
evaluations.reason: Methods A and B both have jina-embeddings-v4 at #1 and GT QwenAmann at #2. Method B's #3 gme-Qwen2-VL is a multimodal retrieval model — all three fit the multimodal retrieval task perfectly. Method A's #3 gte-multilingual-base is text-only embedding, less suited for visual layout encoding. Method C has GT at #1 but Gliese-OCR and nemoretriever-ocr are OCR models, not retrieval models.

evaluations.query: general-purpose instruction-tuned LLM for text generation, abstractive summarization, and extractive QA tasks
evaluations.reason: None include the exact GT Llama-3.2-3B. Method A recommends gpt-oss-120b, Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct, and Qwen3-235B — all powerful instruction-tuned general-purpose LLMs. Method B has Llama-3.1 variants but in quantized/base forms (AWQ-INT4, non-instruct, GGUF) which are less directly usable. Method C has a niche Llama fine-tune, roberta-base-squad2 (extractive QA only), and GENRE (entity retrieval) — fragmented and not general-purpose.

evaluations.query: code LLM with strong reasoning capability for generating frontend code (HTML/CSS/JS) from natural language instructions
evaluations.reason: None include the exact GT Ling-1T. Method B has Octans-Qwen3-UI-Code-4B (specifically for UI code), UIGEN-FX-4B-RL (UI generation), and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B — the best combination for frontend code generation with reasoning. Method A has Octans at #1 plus Ling-flash-2.0 (same family as GT) and MiniMax-M1 (general reasoning, not code-specific). Method C has Octans, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, and CodeLlama-13b — solid but older/smaller code models.

evaluations.query: PII detection and redaction NER model, supports custom entity types for names, phone numbers, account IDs in documents
evaluations.reason: All three have GT gliner-pii-large at #1 or #3. Method B has GT at #1, gliner_medium-v2.1 (supports custom entities via zero-shot) at #2, and gliner-small-pii at #3 — all GLiNER models that support custom entity types. Method C has PII-Model-Phi3 at #1, gliner-small-pii at #2, GT at #3 — all PII-focused. Method A has GT at #1 but distilbert-NER at #2 is a fixed-entity NER model (no custom entities), mismatching the custom entity requirement.
